9                  SOUTHERN DISTRICT OF CALIFORNIA

11  KIMERA LABS INC.,                    Case No. 21-cv-2137-MMA-DDL          

12                             Plaintiff,                                     
                                        ORDER DENYING WITHOUT                
13  v.                                   PREJUDICE COUNSEL’S MOTION           
                                        TO WITHDRAW AS COUNSEL OF            
14  RAJ JAYASHANKAR, et al.,                                                  
                                        RECORD FOR KIMERA LABS INC           
15                          Defendants.                                       
                                        [Doc. No. 361]                       
16                                                                            
17                                                                            
18                                                                            
19                                                                            
20       On November 30, 2024, Plaintiff Kimera Labs Inc.’s (“Plaintiff”) attorneys Peter 
21  T. Mavrick, Esq., Jacob M. Resnick, Esq., Karen Lowell, Esq., and the Mavrick Law 
22  Firm (collectively, the “Mavrick Law Firm Attorneys”) filed a motion to withdraw as 
23  counsel for Plaintiff.  Doc No. 361.                                      
24       “An attorney may not withdraw as counsel except by leave of court.”  Darby v. 
25  City of Torrance, 810 F. Supp. 275, 276 (C.D. Cal. 1992); see also CivLR 83.3(f)(3).  
26  The decision to grant or deny a motion for withdrawal is within the court’s discretion, 
27  and courts consider the following factors: “(1) the reasons why withdrawal is sought; 
28  (2) the prejudice withdrawal may cause to other litigants; (3) the harm withdrawal might 
1    cause to the administration of justice; and (4) the degree to which withdrawal will delay 
2 || the resolution of the case.”  Garrett v. Ruiz, No.  11cv2540-IEG (WVG), 2013 U.S. Dist. 
3  || LEXIS 8053, 2013 WL 163420, at *2 (S.D. Cal. Jan.  14, 2013). 
4         Here, the Mavrick Law Firm Attorneys explain that Kimera has “made it 
5 || unreasonably difficult for counsel to carry out their representation effectively,” but do not 
6 || otherwise support their request for withdrawal.  Doc. No. 361 at 2.  Consequently, the 
7    Court DENIES their motion without prejudice to renewal upon a  sufficient showing of 
8 || entitlement to the relief they seek.  Namely, should the Mavrick Law Firm Attorneys 
9 || renew their request, they must provide adequate factual support (without breaching the 
10 || attorney-client privilege) in support of their request.  Additionally, because the Mavrick 
11        Firm Attorneys suggest that withdrawal would render Plaintiff pro se, they must 
12 || provide clarification on whether Olivia Retenauer, of Mavrick Law Firm, and Jon F. 
13 || Cieslak, of Bona Law PC, also join in their request for withdrawal. 
14         IT IS SO ORDERED. 
15   ||Dated:  December 2, 2024                 “ Wt ll  DA □  Ce “hh 
16                                             HON. MICHAEL M. ANELLO 
17                                             United States District Judge
